# clone

Add a `clone` command that clones a repository and enters it:

```bash
$ clone git@github.com:kamilsk/dotfiles.git
# git clone git@github.com:kamilsk/dotfiles.git
```

— the successor of the `glone` alias idea ([[DOT-140]]), as a function so that the `cd` affects the shell.

<!-- 2026-09-16T05:49Z https://github.com/kamilsk/dotfiles/issues/243#issuecomment-5711691573
Code vs intent: `clone` recognises git sources only by the `git@` prefix; `clone https://github.com/x/y.git` falls through to the file/dir branch, finds nothing, and returns 0 having done nothing. `.git` is stripped with unanchored `sed 's/.git//g'` (dot is a wildcard), mangling names like `digit.git` or `agit`.
-->
